#    Experiment parameters
double experiment(7,1)
       0                   # StartTime    Time at which integration starts
                           #              (and linearization and trimming time)
    1815                   # StopTime     Time at which integration stops
       0                   # Increment    Communication step size, if > 0
     500                   # nInterval    Number of communication intervals, if > 0
  1.0000000000000000E-04   # Tolerance    Relative precision of signals for
                           #              simulation, linearization and trimming
       0                   # MaxFixedStep Maximum step size of fixed step size
                           #              integrators, if > 0.0
       8                   # Algorithm    Integration algorithm as integer (1...28)
                           #
                           #             | model|       |        | dense | state |
                           # Algorithm   | typ  | stiff | order  | output| event |
                           # ------------+------+-------+--------+-------+-------+
                           #  1 | deabm  |  ode |   no  |  1-12  |  yes  |   no  |
                           #  2 | lsode1 |  ode |   no  |  1-12  |  yes  |   no  |
                           #  3 | lsode2 |  ode |  yes  |  1-5   |  yes  |   no  |
                           #  4 | lsodar |  ode |  both |1-12,1-5|  yes  |  yes  |
                           #  5 | dopri5 |  ode |   no  |   5    |   no  |   no  |
                           #  6 | dopri8 |  ode |   no  |   8    |   no  |   no  |
                           #  7 | grk4t  |  ode |  yes  |   4    |   no  |   no  |
                           #  8 | dassl  |  dae |  yes  |  1-5   |  yes  |  yes  |
                           #  9 | odassl | hdae |  yes  |  1-5   |  yes  |  yes  |
                           # 10 | mexx   | hdae |   no  |  2-24  |   no  |   no  |
                           # 11 | euler  |  ode |   no  |   1    |   no  |  yes  |
                           # 12 | rkfix2 |  ode |   no  |   2    |   no  |  yes  |
                           # 13 | rkfix3 |  ode |   no  |   3    |   no  |  yes  |
                           # 14 | rkfix4 |  ode |   no  |   4    |   no  |  yes  |
                           #>=14| others |  ode |yes/no |  2-5   |   yes |  yes  |
                           # ---+--------+------+-------+--------+-------+-------+
                           # euler and rkfix have fixed stepsize.


#    Method tuning parameters
double method(27,1)
       1                   # grid     type of communication time grid, defined by
                           #          = 1: equidistant points ("Increment/nInterval")
                           #          = 2: vector of grid points ("tgrid")
                           #          = 3: variable step integrator (automatically)
                           #          = 4: model (call of "increment" in Dymola, e.g.
                           #                      incr=Time > 2 then 0 else 0.1
                           #                      dummy=increment(incr))
                           #          grid = 1,3 is stopped by "StopTime"
                           #          grid = 2   is stopped by "tgrid(last)"
                           #          grid = 4   runs forever (stopped by model)
       1                   # nt       Use every NT time instant, if grid = 3
       3                   # dense    1/2/3 restart/step/interpolate GRID points
       1                   # evgrid   0/1 do not/save event points in comm. time grid
       1                   # evu      0/1 U-discontinuity does not/trigger events
       0                   # evuord       U-discontinuity order to consider (0,1,...)
       0                   # error    0/1/2 One message/warning/error messages
       0                   # jac      0/1 Compute jacobian numerically/by BLOCKJ
       0                   # xd0c     0/1 Compute/set XD0
       0                   # f3       0/1 Ignore/use F3 of HDAE (= index 1)
       0                   # f4       0/1 Ignore/use F4 of HDAE (= index 2)
       0                   # f5       0/1 Ignore/use F5 of HDAE (= invar.)
       0                   # debug    flags for debug information (1<<0 uses pdebug) 
     100                   # pdebug       priority of debug information (1...100)
       0                   # fmax     Maximum number of evaluations of BLOCKF, if > 0
       0                   # ordmax   Maximum allowed integration order, if > 0
       0                   # hmax     Maximum absolute stepsize, if > 0
       0                   # hmin     Minimum absolute stepsize, if > 0 (use with care!)
       0                   # h0       Stepsize to be attempted on first step, if > 0
  2.0000000000000000E-14   # teps     Bound to check, if 2 equal time instants
  1.0000000000000000E-10   # eveps    Hysteresis epsilon at event points
      20                   # eviter   Maximum number of event iterations
  9.9999999999999995E-07   # delaym   Minimum time increment in delay buffers
       1                   # fexcep   0/1 floating exception crashes/stops dymosim
       1                   # tscale   clock-time = tscale*simulation-time, if grid = 5
                           #          > 1: simulation too slow
                           #          = 1: simulation-time = real-time
                           #          < 1: simulation too fast
       1                   # shared   (not used)
    2473                   # memkey   (not used)

# Matrix with 6 columns defining the initial value calculation
# (columns 5 and 6 are not utilized for the calculation but are
#  reported by dymosim via dymosim -i for user convenience):
#
# column 1: Type of initial value
#           = -2: special case: for continuing simulation (column 2 = value)
#           = -1: fixed value (column 2 = fixed value)
#           =  0: free value, i.e., no restriction (column 2 = initial value)
#           >  0: desired value (column 1 = weight for optimization
#                                column 2 = desired value)
#                 use weight=1, since automatic scaling usually
#                 leads to equally weighted terms
# column 2: fixed, free or desired value according to column 1.
# column 3: Minimum value (ignored, if Minimum >= Maximum).
# column 4: Maximum value (ignored, if Minimum >= Maximum).
#           Minimum and maximum restrict the search range in initial
#           value calculation. They might also be used for scaling.
# column 5: Category of variable.
#           = 1: parameter.
#           = 2: state.
#           = 3: state derivative.
#           = 4: output.
#           = 5: input.
#           = 6: auxiliary variable.
# column 6: Data type of variable and flags according to dsBaseType
#  <value>&3= 0: real.
#  <value>&3= 1: boolean.
#  <value>&3= 2: integer.
#
# Initial values are calculated according to the following procedure:
#
# Initial values are calculated according to the following procedure:
#
# - If parameters, states and inputs are FIXED, and other variables
#   are FREE, the initialization is performed in the normal way.
#
# - If parameters and inputs are FIXED, and all other variables
#   have special case for continue (-2 in 1st column), or FREE
#   the initialization is ignored and variables are set to these values.
#   This is intended to continue the simulation.
#
#   Which variables will be important for initialization and continue
#   is indicated by value in column 6 & dsStartMasks.
#

FirstOrder smoothing time constant on RV07/RV08's Kv command -- opening ramp, same anti-chatter role as firstOrder/firstOrder2 on valve6/valve5 (avoids instantaneous Kv steps). Briefly lowered 8 -> 3 on 2026-09-01 to try to shrink the RV07/RV08 ramp-overlap window in the post-relocation oscillation; reverted the same day -- confirmed worse on every measure (state events 836->1007, CPU 743s->1190s, oscillation period 17.7s->a tighter 14.6s, and 3 genuine 'Failed to solve nonlinear system using Newton solver' warnings appeared that were not present at 8s). The ramp speed was never the actual driver -- it just let the same excess valve authority (KvReliefMax/KvMakeupMax) get applied faster, shortening the bang-bang cycle instead of damping it. Superseded by the 2026-09-01 hysteresis rewrite (see pMakeupOpen/pMakeupClose/pReliefOpen/pReliefClose) which addresses the cycle at its source instead of tuning around it. [s]

RV07's pulse-arming latch. As of the 2026-09-01 split-range rewrite this no longer gates RV07's Kv directly (RV07Limiter runs its small PID trim continuously regardless of makeupActive -- see RV07Limiter's docstring); makeupActive's only remaining job is to arm/cool down the large feedforward PULSE: turns true the instant sensor_p_suction drops to/below pMakeupOpen (arming a pulse, see makeupPulsing), turns false once it recovers to/above pMakeupClose, and a new pulse can't be armed again until that recovery happens -- this is what stops the pulse from re-firing repeatedly while pressure lingers just below pMakeupOpen. This design was arrived at by observing an actual bug: a 2026-09-01 run where makeupActive got stuck true (a when/elsewhen collision, since fixed -- see the git history right above the when-blocks below) accidentally left RV07 running this same always-on continuous trim for the whole run, and that run was dead stable/non-oscillating specifically because a continuously-modulated valve has no discrete state to hunt between, unlike the old hysteresis-gated on/off design. This rewrite makes that behavior deliberate. start is evaluated from the live sensor rather than hardcoded false, so a model that initializes already below pMakeupOpen still latches active instead of the when-clause's crossing edge being missed at t=0 -- see the 2026-09-01 migration-notes entry for why a hardcoded false previously silently disabled RV07/RV08 for an entire run. [:#(type=Boolean)]
True for the first part of a makeupActive episode: RV07 commanded to a large fixed Kv (KvMakeupPulse, not PID-moderated) to deliver makeupPulseTargetMass quickly, added 2026-09-01 to replace running full trim authority for the whole open window (see pMakeupClose's docstring for why that limit-cycled). Set true on the same edge that sets makeupActive; cleared (see the when-clause below) once makeupDeliveredMass reaches makeupPulseTargetMass or sensor_p_suction already reached pMakeupClose, whichever comes first -- after that RV07Limiter drops back to its normal small PID-moderated trim (KvGainMakeup/KvMakeupMax), the same trim that's running continuously at all other times too (see RV07Limiter's docstring). [:#(type=Boolean)]
Estimated helium mass, kg, to admit during the current pulse to bring sensor_p_suction from its value at the triggering instant up to pMakeupClose -- ideal gas law: (pMakeupClose - p_trigger)*V_loopEffective/(R_specificHelium*T_loopEstimate). Recomputed only on the makeupPulsing rising edge (frozen for the rest of the episode); an estimate, not exact -- see V_loopEffective's docstring for why that's fine (the trim phase that follows absorbs the error).
Integral of the actual RV07 loop-side mass flow (abs(RV07.summary.m_flow_gas_B)) since the current pulse started -- see the equation-section der()/reinit pair. Compared against makeupPulseTargetMass to decide when to end the pulse; using the model's own simulated flow (not the Kv/dp estimate that sized the pulse) makes the pulse cutoff self-correcting even if KvMakeupPulse or V_loopEffective/T_loopEstimate are inaccurate.
